steps.tx: The single-rod progestogen implant **Nexplanon subdermal implant** is a four-centimeter flexible ethylene-vinyl acetate rod containing sixty-eight milligrams of etonogestrel, the active metabolite of desogestrel. Inserted subdermally into the inner upper arm, it delivers continuous contraception for three years, boasting the lowest failure rate among reversible methods.
steps.say: Nexplanon is a single-rod subdermal implant providing three years of highly reliable contraception.

vis.alt: Nexplanon subdermal contraceptive rod and preloaded sterile applicator.
vis.caption: Subdermal etonogestrel contraceptive implant rod alongside its insertion applicator. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The primary contraceptive mechanism of the etonogestrel implant is **complete ovulation suppression**. Controlled zero-order release of etonogestrel suppresses hypothalamic GnRH pulsatility and abolishes the pituitary LH surge throughout the three-year duration. High-dose progestin release simultaneously thickens cervical mucus, providing a secondary barrier against ascending spermatozoa.
steps.say: Etonogestrel suppresses the LH surge to arrest ovulation while maintaining impenetrable cervical mucus.

steps.tx: With a Pearl index of 0.05, subdermal implants exhibit **superior contraceptive effectiveness** surpassing male and female surgical sterilisation. Efficacy is completely independent of user compliance, memory, or coital timing. The method is completely reversible, with serum etonogestrel dropping to undetectable levels within one week of surgical removal, restoring baseline ovulatory function.
steps.say: Implants achieve unmatched effectiveness with immediate return of fertility after removal.

left.title: Effectiveness Profile
points: Pearl index is 0.05 pregnancies per 100 WY
Zero user-compliance requirement
Superior to surgical tubectomy

right.title: Reversibility Kinetics
points: Etonogestrel cleared within days of removal
Ovulation resumes in over 90 percent within 3 weeks
No long-term negative impact on future fertility

steps.tx: Placement is performed under local anesthesia in the **non-dominant inner upper arm**. The rod is inserted eight to ten centimeters proximal to the medial humeral epicondyle, placed strictly subdermally in the groove between the biceps and triceps muscles. Clinicians avoid deep insertion into the muscle fascia to prevent neurovascular injury to the ulnar nerve or brachial artery.
steps.say: The implant is inserted strictly subdermally in the upper arm, avoiding deeper neurovascular structures.

left.title: Anatomical Landmarks
points: 8 to 10 cm above medial humeral epicondyle
Sulcus between biceps and triceps muscles
Strictly superficial subdermal plane

right.title: Structures to Avoid
points: Deep muscular fascia of the arm
Basilic vein coursing in medial sulcus
Ulnar and medial cutaneous nerves

steps.tx: To ensure immediate verification of correct placement, the modern Nexplanon rod is **radiopaque on plain radiographs**. Barium sulfate embedded within the core polymer allows detection via soft-tissue X-rays or high-frequency ultrasonography if an implant becomes impalpable. Immediate post-insertion palpation by both clinician and patient is mandatory before applying pressure bandages.
steps.say: Barium sulfate makes the implant radiopaque, allowing radiographic localization if it is non-palpable.

rows: Visualizes superficial and deep soft tissue rods
Rapidly identifies radiopaque barium sulfate core
Identifies deep intramuscular or intravascular migration

steps.tx: The single most common adverse effect leading to elective discontinuation is **unpredictable irregular bleeding**. Approximately twenty percent of women develop amenorrhoea, fifty percent experience infrequent or irregular spotting, and ten percent suffer prolonged bleeding episodes. Because bleeding irregularities are benign and reflect atrophic endometrium, proactive pre-insertion counselling is critical.
steps.say: Unpredictable bleeding is common and requires thorough pre-insertion patient counselling.

left.title: Bleeding Distribution
points: Amenorrhoea in approximately 20 percent
Infrequent light bleeding in 35 percent
Frequent or prolonged bleeding in 15 percent

right.title: Medical Interventions
points: Short course of combined oral contraceptive pills
Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (mefenamic acid)
Tranexamic acid during heavy spotting episodes

steps.tx: Removal of a correctly placed implant is performed under local infiltration using the **pop-up removal technique**. A two-millimeter skin incision is made over the distal tip of the rod. Gentle pressure on the proximal end pushes the distal tip through the incision, where it is grasped with a curved mosquito forceps and extracted.
steps.say: The pop-up technique pushes the distal tip of the rod through a tiny two-millimeter skin incision.

rows: Infiltrate 1 mL lidocaine beneath distal tip
2 mm longitudinal nick over palpable tip
Push proximal end to pop tip forward

steps.tx: According to the WHO medical eligibility criteria, the etonogestrel implant is **category one for smokers and hypertension**. Because it lacks estrogen, it does not elevate cardiovascular, thrombotic, or stroke risks in women over thirty-five. It is also category one for lactating mothers and women with uncomplicated valvular heart disease.
steps.say: The implant avoids estrogen risks, making it safe for smokers, hypertensive patients, and nursing mothers.

left.title: WHO MEC Category 1
points: Cigarette smokers over 35 years of age
Well-controlled chronic hypertension
Superficial venous varicosities

right.title: WHO MEC Category 4
points: Current active breast carcinoma
Unexplained abnormal vaginal bleeding
Severe decompensated hepatic cirrhosis
